how_to_read: A count is **entries or table rows that print a numeric value for a property, before any structure identification, value-kind classification, temperature or form check, or verification** (preregistration sections 3, 7 and 8). Every count is therefore an UPPER bound on usable distinct compounds, and a sum over sources is an upper bound with heavy double counting.

Counts were made by script over the PDF or EPUB text layer, or read off a named table by hand; the method is recorded beside each, with the hand-check error rate where one was measured. Where a figure is a range the range is stated.
Nothing here says a value is **right**. Several held books copy values from one another, and the printed errors in section 4 were found only by comparing sources or reading the rendered page.
A book that prints an enthalpy of formation without saying whether it is measured or calculated is `unlabelled` (preregistration 3.1) and is not a reference by itself.

The counts below are on covered entries only; scaling to all 413 at the covered rate is a factor of 1.26, an estimate and not a count. Entries that are not single organic compounds (a metal in the formula: 8, 6 and 11 in vols 1, 2 and 3 as a lower bound; a polymer or composition keyword in the title: 0, 2 and 4) are included in the counts.

upper_bounds_note: Each row adds the counts of section 3 that could in principle feed the property, scaling the uncovered Klapoetke entries at the covered rate. The sum double-counts every compound two books both print, which is most of the well-known ones, and none of it has passed identity, value-kind, temperature or form checks: it is a ceiling on entries, not an estimate of distinct compounds. The preregistration asks (11.2) whether 300 VERIFIED eligible entities exist per property; that is measurable only after identity resolution in the corpus build. What this table can show is where the ceiling is already below 300.
